prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign SCORPIO: a scorpion seen from directly above, like a scarab on an amulet: a broad segmented body in the centre, eight legs spread evenly at the sides, two claws raised at the top holding a small eight-pointed star between them, and the segmented tail curving up behind the body into a spiral.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, slow concentric ripples and long falling drops of deep water spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. It is an animal: absolutely NO human face. Not menacing: a quiet, watchful jewel of a creature. The sign's nature shows only through form: armoured segments, a taut curve held perfectly still, depth below a calm surface: intensity, loyalty, mystery, renewal.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: bone white, crimson, violet, deep teal. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
